propositions: Inbound link removal never converges when a pair holds two relations simultaneously (blocks + relates_to), because pair-scoped unlink removes the most-recent link while the peer deletion record names a specific relation, causing guard G5 to decline permanently and re-emit on every pass.

Write path is relation-scoped (add_dependency keyed on (target_id, relation)) but remove path is pair-scoped (_get_link_info returns most-recent net-active link for target with no relation filter), creating asymmetry that prevents removal of a specific relation from a double-related pair.

The fix makes removal symmetric with writes by introducing relation-scoped removal seam graph/_links.py::remove_dependency and threading optional relation parameter through _commands/unlink.py and rebar.unlink library facade, while keeping pair-scoped behavior unchanged when no relation is specified (backward compatible).

Reconciler convergence is restored by making _inbound_unlink_one use relation-scoped removal instead of permanently declining in G5; a removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link removes nothing (safety invariant preserved).
Mutation testing confirms the fix: restoring pair-scoped call in _inbound_unlink_one turns convergence tests RED; restoring relation-scoped call turns them GREEN.
